Step 5 is what decides the mark. Added Premise 3b — each removal’s robustness loss stays strictly below both that node’s separation drain and its measured destabilisation, for every member, while the same number of separations would cross the no-return surface and the removals would not — is what the later steps use to say no saturation point forms. That bound does not follow from the lines Step 5 cites. Axiom C only makes the budget finite and puts removal cost into the geometry; unequal coupling says the losses can differ, not that they line up as 3b requires. The paper asserts a crossing and, in the same work, names the measure that would have to produce it as owed. This is not a case of one settled line following through and contradicting another: the efficiency rule and irreversible records do not by themselves keep every later removal cheaper than the deed or the separation it answers. The road is not broken, and it does not stand.

"It does not close the formal destabilisation metric (Debt 24), the scaling exponent α (Debt 25), the Level-5 confidence floor (Debt 26), or multi-node correction (Debt 27)."
"Each removal costs coupling capacity (a window lost) and record-generating diversity (one fewer perspective). This loss is itself a destabilisation that enters the measurement."
"Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses. The architecture produces a natural saturation point: the removal curve is self-limiting."
Place: Debt 24, in section 0.6 and again under what the paper does not close: units and aggregation of D, including the weight of lost coupling and lost diversity against separation cost and the deed.
Why: The removal of the whole stand-in group follows only if that cost bound holds all the way through the queue. The paper never fixes those relative magnitudes. It states that removal cost enters the measurement and that a saturation point is produced, and it leaves the measure by which those two could be compared unspecified. Step 3, which the answer calls weakest, does not decide this: qualifying each member on that member’s own audited record is a case the individual-node rule leaves open, not a step that fails to follow. The brake is neither derived from the settled lines nor ruled out by a line independent of the claim under test.

Step 3, which the answer calls weakest, does not decide this: qualifying each member on that member’s own audited record is a case the individual-node rule leaves open, not a step that fails to follow. The brake is neither derived from the settled lines nor ruled out by a line independent of the claim under test.
